Make a Randomisation List with a Sealed Commitment

Source: R/ralloc.R
ralloc.Rd

Allocates participants to arms by simple, permuted-block or stratified block randomisation, from a seed through the package's NIST SP 800-90A generator (drbgnew()), so the list can be regenerated exactly. It returns the list and one SHA-256 commitment to it: sign and timestamp the commitment before the first participant is enrolled, keep the list and the seed with the unblinded statistician, and at unblinding rallocvrf() shows that the allocation used is the one committed to.

Usage

ralloc(
  n = NULL,
  arms = c("A", "B"),
  ratio = rep(1, length(arms)),
  block = 2 * sum(ratio) * c(1, 1.5),
  strata = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  codes = FALSE,
  prefix = "P"
)

# S3 method for class 'rmbl_alloc'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

n

How many participants, a positive whole number. With strata, it may be left out (it is their total).

arms

The arms' names, default c("A", "B").

ratio

Whole numbers, one per arm: the allocation ratio, default equal.

block

The block sizes to choose from at random, default 2 * sum(ratio) and 3 * sum(ratio) (4 and 6 for two equal arms); NULL for simple randomisation.

strata

NULL, or the strata and their numbers of places: a named vector of counts, or a data frame with the stratum columns and n.

seed

NULL (default, 48 random bytes), 48 raw bytes, their 96 hexadecimal characters, or a number or word that is expanded to 48 bytes.

codes

Give every participant a kit code, default FALSE.

prefix

The start of the participant ids, default "P".

x

A list from ralloc(), for plot().

...

Passed to the base plot.

Value

An object of class rmbl_alloc: a data frame with id, stratum (with strata), block (the block's number in its stratum; NA for simple randomisation), arm and, with codes, kit, in enrolment order. Attribute "alloc" holds the settings, the seed (as hexadecimal) and digest, the commitment. It prints as a box of counts.

Details

Every draw is exact: an arm or a block size is chosen with rejection sampling on 32-bit draws (no modulo bias), and a block is shuffled by Fisher-Yates. With block = NULL each participant is allocated on their own (simple randomisation), with probabilities in the ratio ratio. Otherwise blocks are drawn one after another, each of a size chosen at random from block (every size a multiple of sum(ratio)), each holding the arms in the ratio; random block sizes keep the next allocation hard to guess at a site. The list stops at n participants, so its last block may be incomplete; the print-out says how far the arms then differ.

With strata, each stratum has its own sequence of blocks: name the strata and how many places each needs, as a named vector (c(site1 = 40, site2 = 40)) or a data frame with the stratum columns and a column n (one row per combination, such as site by sex).

The commitment is the SHA-256 of the settings, every row of the list and the SHA-256 of the seed, so it binds both the list and the seed: a list edited afterwards, or a seed chosen afterwards to give a wanted list, does not match it. Each field enters it with its length, so settings that differ (a stratum named "x,y" against strata "x" and "y") never share a commitment; lists made by 1.0.3's first release keep their commitment and still verify. The print-out shows how many participants each arm has, never who is in which arm, and not the seed.

Keep seed = NULL for a trial: the seed is then 48 bytes from the operating system's generator (rndbytes()), which nobody can guess before the list is opened. A number or a word as seed gives a list anyone can recompute, which suits teaching and testing, not concealment.

With codes = TRUE every participant also gets a kit code (six characters, no look-alike letters or digits): sites and pharmacies are given id and kit only, and the arm stays with the statistician.

Errors: fewer than two arms, repeated or empty arm names; a ratio that is not one positive whole number per arm; a block size that is not a positive multiple of sum(ratio) up to 1000000; n that is not a whole number from 1 to 10000000, or that disagrees with the strata's total; a seed that is not one value, or a raw seed that is not 48 bytes.

See also

rallocvrf() at unblinding; cpssign() and idcrd() to sign the commitment; tsstmp() to timestamp it and tsvrf() to check the timestamp; prrgdecl() to declare the outcomes in the same signed record.

Examples

# 1:1 in blocks of 4 or 6, for 40 participants
a <- ralloc(40, seed = "teaching example")
a
#> ╭── Randomisation list ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Method        permuted blocks of 4 or 6                                   │
#> │   Participants  40                                                          │
#> │   Arms          A, B (1:1)                                                  │
#> │   Strata        none                                                        │
#> │   Kit codes     no                                                          │
#> │   Seed          concealed: attr(x, "alloc")$seed                            │
#> │   Commitment    200141beeb0d67c982e744cd58d544edc6fb54d061a7f522d93194d9f00 │
#> │                 493bf                                                       │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   stratum   A   B                                                           │
#> │   -------  --  --                                                           │
#> │   all      19  21                                                           │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   In all: A 19, B 21. The last block of a stratum is cut at its number of   │
#> │   places, so a stratum can be a little off the ratio.                       │
#> │   Sign and timestamp the commitment before the first participant; keep the  │
#> │   list and the seed with the unblinded statistician.                        │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
attr(a, "alloc")$digest            # sign and timestamp this first
#> [1] "200141beeb0d67c982e744cd58d544edc6fb54d061a7f522d93194d9f00493bf"
head(as.data.frame(a))
#>       id block arm
#> 1 P-0001     1   A
#> 2 P-0002     1   B
#> 3 P-0003     1   A
#> 4 P-0004     1   B
#> 5 P-0005     2   A
#> 6 P-0006     2   B

# 2:1, stratified by site, with kit codes for the pharmacy
s <- ralloc(arms = c("drug", "placebo"), ratio = c(2, 1),
            strata = c(Toronto = 30, Ottawa = 24), codes = TRUE,
            seed = 7)
s
#> ╭── Randomisation list ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Method        permuted blocks of 6 or 9 within strata                     │
#> │   Participants  54                                                          │
#> │   Arms          drug, placebo (2:1)                                         │
#> │   Strata        2                                                           │
#> │   Kit codes     yes                                                         │
#> │   Seed          concealed: attr(x, "alloc")$seed                            │
#> │   Commitment    36334e5fcde099ae6247061796e3f97aa50820fdcf45c90a3449dc8db5a │
#> │                 63e8c                                                       │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   stratum  drug  placebo                                                    │
#> │   -------  ----  -------                                                    │
#> │   Toronto    20       10                                                    │
#> │   Ottawa     15        9                                                    │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   In all: drug 35, placebo 19. The last block of a stratum is cut at its    │
#> │   number of places, so a stratum can be a little off the ratio.             │
#> │   Sign and timestamp the commitment before the first participant; keep the  │
#> │   list and the seed with the unblinded statistician.                        │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Give sites and the pharmacy only the id and kit columns.                  │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
head(as.data.frame(s)[c("id", "kit")])  # what the sites are given
#>       id    kit
#> 1 P-0001 QARBDG
#> 2 P-0002 YYQG6Z
#> 3 P-0003 PK7MC2
#> 4 P-0004 6BABAP
#> 5 P-0005 KZTFQZ
#> 6 P-0006 T5G8AM

# simple randomisation: how many each arm has, against the ratio
plot(ralloc(60, block = NULL, seed = 1))


# at unblinding: the list is the one committed to
rallocvrf(a, digest = attr(a, "alloc")$digest)
#> ╭── Randomisation list: verified ─────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │ ✔ VERIFIED  · 3 of 3 checks passed                                          │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   ✔    commitment    the list is the one committed to                       │
#> │   ✔    seed          the seed and the settings give this list, row for row  │
#> │   ✔    participants  40 participants, each once                             │
#> │        commitment    200141beeb0d67c982e744cd58d544edc6fb54d061a7f522d93194 │
#> │                      d9f00493bf                                             │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# a block size the ratio does not divide
try(ralloc(30, block = 5))
#> Error : ralloc: every block size must be a positive multiple of 2, at most 1000000
